techniques.name: Dual Coding
techniques.description: The use of both verbal and visual information to enhance learning. Combining words and visuals helps students understand and retain information better.
tasks: Use diagrams, illustrations, and graphic organizers alongside verbal explanations.
Encourage students to create their own visual representations.

techniques.name: Worked Examples
techniques.description: Step-by-step demonstrations of how to perform a task or solve a problem. They help students understand the process and reduce cognitive load.
tasks: Provide worked examples for complex problems.
Gradually fade support as students gain confidence and competence.
Encourage students to explain the steps in their own words.

techniques.name: I-We-You Method
techniques.description: A gradual release of responsibility framework where the teacher models the task ('I'), practices it with students ('We'), and then students practice independently ('You').
tasks: Move to guided practice with the class.
Have students practice independently to reinforce learning.

techniques.name: Cognitive Load Management
techniques.description: Strategies to reduce unnecessary cognitive load and optimize working memory during learning tasks. It involves breaking information into smaller chunks and reducing extraneous load.
tasks: Provide scaffolding to support student understanding.

techniques.name: Conceptual Modelling
techniques.description: Creating abstract representations of complex ideas to help students understand and organize information. This can include diagrams, flowcharts, and other visual tools.
tasks: Use conceptual models to explain abstract concepts.
